title: POC orchestration runbook and stakeholder calendar
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook organizes a customer POC from kickoff through acceptance and the two-day on-site/remote workshop. Focus is on producing a minimum deployable integration that demonstrates latency, failover, and cost heuristics for the customer’s production traffic profile.

Primary objectives:
- Deliver a stable POC endpoint running Redwood-hosted model variants with a baseline 99th percentile latency target aligned to customer SLAs.
- Validate model quality (precision/recall or domain-specific metric) against the customer-provided evaluation set.
- Demonstrate autoscaling, canary rollout, and graceful fallback to lower-cost variants in the event of capacity or QoS issues.
- Produce a handoff pack with runbook, dashboard links, and a short operational run-through video.

Success criteria (must be measurable):
1) Functional: End-to-end integration demo that handles 95% of synthetic workload without errors.
2) Latency: 95th percentile within target — customer target is 400ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) in region eu-west-1.
3) Cost envelope: token/unit cost within 25% of forecasted model economics.
4) Quality: Model quality delta vs baseline < 5% on customer test set (metric: F1 or BLEU as agreed).
5) Observability: Dashboard with token-level cost, latency heatmaps, and alerting configured.

Stakeholders and RACI (quick reference):
- Customer PO: Amira Haddad (customer) — Responsible for acceptance and providing eval data.
- Solutions Lead: Priya Menon — Accountable for overall POC delivery.
- Deployment Engineer: Ethan Caldwell — Responsible for infra, model routing, and logging hooks.
- ML Lead: María Ortiz — Responsible for model selection, quantization guidance, and quality checks.
- SRE Liaison: Samir Rao — Responsible for uptime targets, SLOs, and incident playbook.
- CS Engagement: Ava Chen — Customer-facing coordination, meetings, feedback capture.

High-level timeline (6 weeks recommended, compressed options below):
Week 0 (pre-kickoff, ~3–7 days prior):
- Customer to share sample traffic traces and evaluation dataset.
- Solutions team validates access, prepares account, lands API key, whitelists IPs.
- Workshop logistics: invite calendar, runbook draft shared.

Week 1 (kickoff + rapid prototype):
- Day 1: Kickoff call (30–45m) — review scope, acceptance criteria, constraints.
- Day 2–5: Rapid prototype — ingest eval data, spin up test endpoint, smoke tests.
- Deliverable: prototype endpoint + initial latency/cost snapshot.

Week 2 (stability and load shaping):
- Integrate workload replay from customer traces.
- Configure batching and KV cache settings; iterate to meet latency SLOs.
- Deliverable: performance report and recommended batch/cache config.

Week 3 (workshop prep + canary):
- Prepare two variants (high-throughput and high-quality).
- Canary rollout plan defined; rollback criteria documented.
- Mock run of workshop demo.

Week 4 (workshop week):
- Day 1: Technical deep-dive (architecture, routing, observability, failure demos).
- Day 2: Hands-on lab — customer engineers run through deployment, scale tests.
- Deliverable: Workshop notes, action items, observed regressions.

Week 5 (hardening and acceptance testing):
- Run acceptance test suite against production-like load.
- Fix regressions; capture quality metrics.
- Deliverable: Acceptance report and signoff draft.

Week 6 (handoff):
- Final handoff package: runbook, dashboard links, alerts, short video walkthrough.
- Optional: project retrospective and closeout meeting.

Compressed 2–3 week option (if customer timeboxed):
- Collapse prototype + load shaping into week 1, run workshop end of week 2, acceptance by week 3.
- Tradeoffs: less time for genetic tuning and canary burn-in. Note these tradeoffs in the commercial proposal.

Workshop agenda (2-day remote-friendly):
Day 1 — 09:00–12:00: architecture + integration
- Intro and goals (15m)
- Architecture walkthrough: model catalog, routing, and region failover (30m)
- Observability deep-dive: cost/latency dashboards, traces, and alert logic (30m)
- Live demo: endpoint, streaming, and fallback (45m)
- Q&A and breakouts (30m)

Day 1 — 13:00–16:00: lab prep + hands-on
- Lab environment setup guide (20m)
- Developer tasks: call endpoint, inspect headers/traces, trigger fallback (2h)
- Collect feedback and issue log (40m)

Day 2 — 09:00–12:00: scale and resilience
- Load shaping examples and configuration levers (45m)
- Chaos scenarios: region failover, model variant OOM, degraded network (60m)
- Recovery and rollback patterns (45m)

Day 2 — 13:00–16:00: acceptance and next steps
- Run acceptance scenarios (1h)
- Roadmap conversation: Dedicated vs Private fit (30m)
- Closeout: handoff checklist and action items (30m)

Pre-work checklist for customer (send 7–10 days before kickoff):
- Provide sample traffic traces (ideally 1k–10k requests) and an eval set with labels.
- Share network allowlist and test account access.
- Identify a technical point of contact for the workshop.
- Confirm attendee list and time zone constraints.

Infra & access prerequisites (for Solutions team):
- Create test deployment in customer project or Redwood sandbox.
- Configure logging sinks and dashboard access (Grafana/Console links).
- Prepare two model variants (quantized variant + fp16 baseline).
- Pre-provision capacity for scale tests (burst capacity reservation).

Task tracker (template – ongoing update):
- TODO: ingest eval dataset into test bucket — owner: Ethan — due: W1D2 — status: open
- TODO: baseline latency sweep (no batching) — owner: María — due: W1D4 — status: open

- TODO: workshop slides + lab instructions — owner: Priya — due: W3D3 — status: open

Quick runbook: incident steps during POC (short version)
1) Detect: pager or dashboard alert fires for latency > SLO for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
2) Triage: check model variant logs, gateway errors, and region health (SRE).
3) Mitigate: shift traffic to fallback variant / alternate region; notify customer.
4) Fix: adjust batching/cache knobs or restart problematic workers.
5) Postmortem: capture root cause, time to mitigation, and follow-up tasks.

Known risks and mitigations (notes to self):
- Risk: customer eval set too small / biased — Mitigate: request stratified samples and run synthetic augmentation.
- Risk: network ACLs block test traffic — Mitigate: early pre-kickoff network test and whitelisting.
- Risk: model regressions when quantized — Mitigate: reserve fallback unquantized variant and measure delta early.
- Risk: tight calendar — Mitigate: offer asynchronous lab options and recorded walkthroughs.

Acceptance test checklist (example items):
- Smoke test: endpoint returns 200 for 100 consecutive requests.
- Latency: 95th percentile under target in replayed workload.
- Quality: validation suite KPI within threshold.
- Observability: dashboard shows token-level cost, alerts trigger on injected failure.

Handoff deliverables (minimum):
- Runbook doc (this plus finalized checklists)
- Dashboard links and saved queries
- Recorded 20–30m run-through video for ops team
- Action item list with owners and dates (30–60 day follow-up)

Notes & freeform items (brain dump):
- Consider adding an automated script to replay the customer traffic with token-level sampling to estimate cost sensitivity to prompt length.
- If customer is sensitive to egress, document region-specific options and encryption-at-rest notes.
- Keep canary window at least 4 hours at low ramp for production-like validation.

Meeting templates (for daily stand during POC):
- Yesterday: what was validated
- Today: blockers and experiments running
- Risks: anything customer escalated
- Ask: approvals needed (eg, reserve more burst capacity)

Action items (initial):
- Priya: confirm kickoff time with customer and send pre-work list (due: 2024-11-12)
- Ethan: create sandbox deployment and share endpoint (due: 2024-11-14)
- María: run quality baseline and share report (due: 2024-11-15)
- Samir: pre-configure alerting and on-call rotation for POC window (due: 2024-11-18)

Endnotes:
- Keep this doc as the living single-source-of-truth for the engagement. Update the task tracker after each sync with the customer.
- If a commercial change is requested (scope creep), record it in PROJ-2387 and escalate to sales for pricing adjustment.
